title: Isomorphism spaces of a Deligne--Mumford stack are unramified
statement:
Let $S$ and $T$ be schemes [def-pc-scheme], with $T$ an $S$-scheme, and let $\mathcal X$ be a Deligne--Mumford stack over $S$ in the etale-stack and scheme-atlas convention of [def-sfb-stable-pointed-moduli-groupoids]. For any $x,y\in\mathcal X(T)$, the functor on $T$-schemes
$$v:T'\to T\quad\longmapsto\quad\operatorname{Isom}_{\mathcal X(T')}(v^*x,v^*y)$$
is represented by an algebraic space $I$ over $T$ [def-trf-algebraic-space]. Its structure map $I\to T$ is unramified: for every representable etale scheme chart $V\to I$, the composite $V\to T$ is an unramified morphism of schemes [def-weil-unramified-morphism]. Etale scheme charts have the meaning of [def-trf-algebraic-space, def-weil-etale-morphism].

source.place: Tags 06N3 (theorem-DM), direction (3) implies (1), and 06MB (lemma-properties-covering-imply-diagonal), part (1); Isom as a base change of the diagonal: algebraic.tex Tag 045G (lemma-representable-diagonal); base-change stability: spaces-morphisms.tex Tag 03ZJ (lemma-base-change-unramified). These statements are used in the etale-stack convention through the atlas and Isom-space formulation.

proof.text: Use the given etale atlas as a smooth atlas: Mathlib Etale implies Smooth on every scheme chart. Apply lem-sfb-unramified-diagonal-etale-atlas to obtain HasUnramifiedModuliDiagonal F.

Construct cartesian sections associated with x and y by the fibered-category lifting property. Obtain Z over T times T representing the iso-comma category from the unramified diagonal. A vertical natural isomorphism between functors into a discrete moduli category makes those functors equal. Transport the representing equivalence along these equalities so its two projections are exactly the prescribed projections. For each pair q,r of scheme maps, evaluate its comparison isomorphism at a section of Z over (q,r). Full faithfulness proves injectivity: an arrow between two equal comparison objects lifts uniquely to a vertical arrow between sections, which forces equality. Essential surjectivity proves surjectivity: take a preimage of the prescribed comparison object and pull its section back by the inverse of its base isomorphism. The comma square gives the prescribed comparison. Naturality follows by the comma square of the restriction arrow.

source.place: Tag 04SI, explicit identification of the isomorphism sheaf as a 2-fibre product; algebraic.tex Tag 045G

proof.text: Form the actual sheaf pullback I = Z times_(T times T) T along the diagonal. It is an algebraic space by lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers; the representable scheme sheaf is an algebraic space by lem-trf-space-enlarged-etale-ringed-site-model. Its pointwise pullback universal property and Yoneda identify sections over q with sections of Z over (q,q). Compose with the bijections of step 2. Compare arbitrary cartesian lifts with the chosen ones by their unique cartesian isomorphisms. Conjugation gives the required bijections for all lifts. Cartesian uniqueness and associativity give the displayed restriction equation.

Verify unramifiedness of I over T by pulling back a representable surjective etale scheme atlas of Z. The resulting atlas of I is the base change of the unramified scheme map from the atlas of Z to T times T, so is unramified over T by Mathlib base-change stability of locally finite type and formally unramified morphisms. For any etale scheme chart V of I, represent its pullback of this atlas by E. Both chart projections are etale, and E to V is surjective. Precomposition and the pointwise source-and-target locality criterion from lem-sfb-scheme-unramified-etale-locality imply that V to T is unramified. Representability and etaleness of the pullback use lem-trf-space-chartwise-etale-permanence.
